Chapter 3 · Tips 21–30

Problem-Solving, Communication, and Value

问题解决、沟通与价值

Project Management Is Problem Management项目管理就是问题管理

Lorin Unger · Hoboken, New Jersey, U.S.Lorin Unger · 美国新泽西州霍博肯

IN THE BEST OF CIRCUMSTANCES, software project management is a challenging and complex endeavor. Yet, I often see PMs make it even more difficult by having the wrong set of expectations for the role. Plain and simple, project management is problem management. Were that not the case, there would be no need for project managers. Rather, a request for execution would be made and all the pieces (resources, technology, requirements, timeline, etc.) would simply align and the work would proceed smoothly to completion without any need for shepherding.

即便在最好的情况下，软件项目管理也是一项充满挑战的复杂工作。可我常看到项目经理因为对这个角色抱错了期待，把事情搞得更难。说白了，项目管理就是问题管理。若非如此，根本不需要项目经理——只要下达一个执行指令，所有要素（资源、技术、需求、工期等）自然会各就各位，工作一路顺畅到收尾，根本不需要人来牵线。

The truth is, our role exists because that is not the reality. Resources are overallocated, technologies and skill sets are incompatible, requirements are unclear, and timelines are unrealistic. I frequently work with PMs who view those types of issues as inconveniences, annoyances, or "problems" caused by external forces that are interfering with their work. If only they had done this, if only they had thought that out better, if only they would give me more time, then all these needless complications would be gone and I could finally get on with the business of project management. Needless to say, these folks spend a lot of their time frustrated, tense, and irritable.

事实是，我们这个角色之所以存在，正因为现实并非如此。资源被过度分配，技术与技能不匹配，需求含糊不清，工期不切实际。我常和一些项目经理共事，他们把这些问题视为外来干扰造成的不便、烦心或"麻烦"。只要他们当时做了这个，只要他们把那个想得更周全，只要他们多给我点时间，这些无谓的复杂就会消失，我终于能好好做项目管理了。不用说，这类人大部分时间都在挫败、紧绷和烦躁中度过。

— p.68 —

The fact of the matter is, smoothing all those needless bumps and complications is the business of project management. Our role is to plan better, think more clearly, and have a greater strategic vision than those who sponsor a project, and also those who work to deliver it. We're here because executing a project is an inherently messy business and individuals with our unique skills and temperaments are necessary to ensure that the inevitable difficulties get squashed, circumvented, or massaged into nonissues.

事实是，把这些无谓的磕绊和复杂捋顺，就是项目管理这门生意。我们的角色就是要比项目发起人、比交付团队规划得更好、想得更清楚、更有战略眼光。我们之所以在这里，是因为执行项目本质上就是一团乱麻，需要有我们这种独特技能和气质的人，来把不可避免的困难压下去、绕过去，或者揉搓成"不是问题"。

To complicate things further, this does not apply only to the mechanics of managing a project. Sometimes people need to be "massaged into nonissues" as well. The most challenging aspect of a project isn't necessarily the technology or timeline, but can be the personalities involved in the effort. This can be anyone from resources assigned to the project to a senior oversight committee. Some easy archetypes: the "resentful resource," who seems perversely committed to undermining the PM's authority; the "nervous stakeholder," ever anxious, is impossible to soothe; or the "back-seat PM," a stakeholder or project participant who feels compelled to assert his/her opinion on how the project should be run at every possible opportunity.

更麻烦的是，这不只适用于项目管理的"机制"层面。有时候人也需要被"揉搓成不是问题"。项目最有挑战的部分未必是技术或工期，而可能是参与其中的各色人等。可以是被派到项目上的任何资源，也可以是高级监督委员会。几个典型原型："愤愤不平的资源"，一门心思破坏项目经理的权威；"神经紧张的相关方"，永远焦虑，怎么都安抚不下来；或者"后排项目经理"，逮着机会就要对项目该怎么搞指手画脚。

It is, of course, beyond the scope of this tip to discuss how best to manage the various interpersonal issues that can arise in a project. Suffice it to say that the need to manage issues in this realm appears frequently, and is as much within the scope of our project management responsibilities as is understanding the work breakdown structure or maintaining an accurate project plan. If we view these situations not as obstacles to doing the job but, more appropriately, as the heart of the job itself, the work will be smoother, calmer, and more tranquil. Relatively speaking, of course.

当然，如何最好地处理项目中可能出现的各种人际问题，不是这篇短文能讲完的。只需说：在这个领域管理问题的需要频繁出现，它和理解工作分解结构、维护准确的项目计划一样，都属于我们项目管理职责的范围。如果我们不把这些情况看作"干活的障碍"，而更恰当地看作"工作本身的核心"，工作就会更顺、更平静、更安宁——当然，是相对而言。

— p.69 —

Empowering Developers: A Man Named Tim赋能开发：一个叫 Tim 的人

Ken Sipe · St. Charles, Missouri, U.S.Ken Sipe · 美国密苏里州圣查尔斯

OFTEN THE BEST THING a software project manager can do is set the vision, set the priorities, and get out of the way. Here's a true story about a man named Tim. We found we needed another team member on our project, so we posted the opening and began to interview. One individual soon rose to the top of our candidate list.

软件项目经理能做的最好的事，往往是：定好愿景、排好优先级，然后让开路。讲一个关于 Tim 的真实故事。我们发现项目还需要一个人，于是发布职位、开始面试。有个人很快排在了候选人名单榜首。

His name was Tim. Tim stood out significantly from the other applicants, and it would have been a "no-brainer" decision to hire him. But, there was one dissenting vote. All resources hired into our department may rotate between any one of three project managers. One of those PMs had previous experience working with Tim and indicated that he lacked motivation. She painted a picture of Tim web surfing regularly while on the job, and being a slacker.

他叫 Tim。Tim 明显比其他候选人突出，招他本来是个"不用想"的决定。但有一票反对。我们部门招进来的人，可能在三位项目经理之间轮换。其中一位以前和 Tim 共事过，说他缺乏动力。她描述的 Tim 是：上班经常刷网页，是个懒鬼。

This was a tough situation. When making a hiring decision, more weight would normally be applied to a project manager's personal experience with the candidate as compared to a cold interview. However, from a technical perspective, Tim's skills significantly exceeded those of other candidates. He was hired despite the dissenting vote. The project was run using an agile development methodology, so we had an open meeting at the start of the iteration. The opening meeting has several main purposes:

这局面很棘手。做招聘决策时，通常一位项目经理与候选人的私交体验，比一次冷冰冰的面试分量更重。但从技术角度看，Tim 的能力远超其他候选人。尽管有反对票，他还是被招了进来。项目用敏捷开发方法论运行，所以在迭代开始时我们开了一个开放会议。启动会有几个主要目的：

* Iteration: A short period chosen by an agile team (a week, two weeks, a month, etc.) during which a key requirement chosen by the customer is developed, tested, and delivered for approval. The next iteration then begins on the next most important requirement.* 迭代：敏捷团队选定的一小段时间（一周、两周、一个月等），在此期间开发、测试并交付客户选定的一项关键需求供其批准。下一个迭代再开始处理下一项最重要的需求。

† Story: A high-level description of a software requirement, usually broken down into single developer tasks, with just enough information to allow a developer to estimate how long it will take to create, test, and/or implement it.† 用户故事（Story）：对软件需求的高层描述，通常拆成单个开发任务，信息刚好够开发估算创建、测试和实现所需的时间。

  • Stories are created and their priority is established and communicated, based on user input.
    根据用户输入创建用户故事，确定并沟通其优先级。
  • A team vision of the project scope is created through the stories, and good acceptance criteria are established.
    通过故事形成对项目范围的团队共识，并建立良好的验收标准。
  • Stories are broken down into tasks and estimated by the developer who is to complete the task.
    故事拆成任务，由要完成任务的开发本人估算。
— p.70 —

After the meeting, the tasks are entered into the task tracking system. The significance of the task tracking system is often misunderstood. It is used for developers to see what tasks are started. If they have finished their own tasks early, they move on by "stealing" (or completing) a task not yet begun by the originally assigned developer.

会后，任务录入任务跟踪系统。任务跟踪系统的意义常被误解。它是给开发看哪些任务已经开始的。如果自己的任务提前做完，他们就"偷"（也就是完成）那个原本分配给别人、还没开始的任务。

Tim turned out to be an outstanding hire. He out-produced everyone else on the team. The most obvious measure of his value was in the number of tasks he "stole" from other developers. Completing more tasks meant the project finished quicker.

Tim 结果成了一笔出色的招聘。他的产出超过团队里所有人。衡量他价值最直观的指标，就是他从别人那里"偷"走的任务数量。完成的任务越多，项目收尾越快。

So the question is, why would another PM see Tim as unproductive? On closer inspection, it became evident that the Tim-basher had a management style that was excessively controlling. She would "spoon-feed" tasks to developers and then leave the team workspace to attend meetings. Tim was so fast that he would complete his assigned task immediately. Without any further direction regarding project priorities or tasks he could begin next, he was left idle.

那么问题来了：为什么另一位项目经理会觉得 Tim 不出活？仔细一看就明白，那个黑 Tim 的人管理风格过度控制。她把任务"一口一口喂"给开发，然后离开团队工位去开会。Tim 太快了，立刻就把分配的任务做完。没有进一步的项目优先级指示，也没有告诉他下一个能开始什么任务，他就闲在那里了。

You'll be amazed what a good team can do with a clear vision, well-defined acceptance criteria, and shared project priorities not determined by a lone software project manager but known, documented, and managed by the entire team. Sometimes the best thing for the PM to do is get out of the way. Do you manage a Tim?

当一个好团队有清晰的愿景、明确的验收标准、以及由整个团队共同知晓、记录和管理（而非由单个项目经理独断）的共享项目优先级时，你会惊讶于他们能做出什么。有时候项目经理最好的做法就是让开路。你手下也有一个 Tim 吗？

— p.71 —

Clever Code Is Hard to Maintain聪明的代码难维护

David Wood · Fredericksburg, Virginia, U.S.David Wood · 美国弗吉尼亚州弗雷德里克斯堡

DEVELOPERS ARE OFTEN ASKED TO CREATE MIRACLES. They must find clever ways to make today's project code work with yesterday's antiquated legacy software containing multiple patches. And through skill and ingenuity, they may create numerous lines of clever code that finally get the job done. But clever code may only create future maintenance problems due to the code's length and complexity. There may be a better way.

开发常被要求创造奇迹。他们必须找到巧妙的办法，让今天的项目代码跑在昨天那套打了一堆补丁的陈旧遗留软件上。靠着技术和巧思，他们也许能写出大量聪明的代码，终于把活干完。但聪明的代码可能只是因为太长、太复杂，给未来的维护制造麻烦。也许有更好的办法。

If you are a project manager new to software development, don't be afraid to let developers explore new languages and development tools. Allow them this freedom, because this is how they discover innovative ways to improve their coding practices and results. They may be able to design a software solution to your legacy interface problem that is faster and has fewer lines of code to test and maintain. This is certainly an advantage to your project.

如果你是刚接触软件开发的项目经理，别怕让开发探索新语言和开发工具。给他们这份自由，因为他们正是这样发现改进编码实践和成果的创新方法。他们也许能为你的遗留接口问题设计出一个更快、待测试和维护代码更少的软件方案。这对你的项目无疑是优势。

There are innovative new programming languages that can perform the same functions as your current ones with substantially fewer lines of code. This is valuable in that a simpler code structure is easier to test, can be self-defining, is smaller to store, and is easier to maintain.

有些创新的新编程语言，能用少得多的代码实现与现有语言相同的功能。这很有价值：更简单的代码结构更容易测试、可以自解释、存储更小、也更容易维护。

Obviously, there are some concerns about adding new languages and platforms within your organization. Will this new code truly solve the problem for the current software or upgrade under development? Will it interface long-term with the existing software used in your legacy databases, user interfaces within the organization, and third-party software in which the company has already invested?

显然，在组织里引入新语言和新平台会有一些顾虑。这段新代码真的能解决当前正在开发的软件或升级的问题吗？它能长期与你遗留数据库中用的现有软件、组织内部的用户界面、以及公司已经投资的第三方软件对接吗？

— p.72 —

Are there other developers on the team or the department who will be able to create software in this language or on this platform? Is there adequate product support from language authors? Will there be timely updates and improvements? Even if you are not familiar with programming yourself, don't be reluctant to allow programmers to embrace new languages. If the new language can trace its tortured lineages back to C or Java (or any other common way of doing things), it is probably going to be relatively painless to merge it into your current practices.

团队或部门里还有别的开发能用这门语言、这个平台写软件吗？语言作者提供足够的产品支持吗？会有及时的更新和改进吗？即使你自己不懂编程，也不要舍不得让程序员拥抱新语言。如果这门新语言能把它曲折的谱系追溯到 C 或 Java（或任何其他常见套路），那把它融入你现有的实践大概不会太痛。

However, be sure to document any new practices within your code. Otherwise, your code base and the documentation about the code may diverge to the point that the best way to understand the system is to look at the code itself. This is called a "loss of coupling" between the software components and system metadata. And when there is inadequate documentation to maintain your software system, it must be replaced.

但是，一定要在代码中记录任何新做法。否则，代码库和代码文档会偏离到"理解系统最好的办法就是直接看代码"的地步。这叫做软件组件与系统元数据之间的"耦合丧失"。而当文档不足以维护你的软件系统时，系统就必须被替换。

Encourage your project team developers to be innovative, but not clever to the point of excessive complexity. Being too clever makes it hard on those who follow. If later developers can't read the code, how can they be expected to maintain it? Any given programmer may try to be clever to enhance his job security, but no project manager will benefit from it. Code that is too clever will ultimately be too hard to maintain. That leads to maintenance failure and a costly reworking of your software systems.

鼓励项目团队的开发创新，但不要聪明到过度复杂。太聪明会让后来者难受。如果后来的开发读不懂代码，怎么指望他们维护？某个程序员可能想靠耍聪明来增加自己的职场安全感，但没有哪个项目经理会从中受益。太聪明的代码最终会难到无法维护。那会导致维护失败，并让你付出高昂代价去重做软件系统。

— p.73 —

Managing Human Factors in IT Project ManagementIT 项目管理中的人的因素

James Graham, PMP · Ta' l-Ibrag, MaltaJames Graham（PMP）· 马耳他

AS SOFTWARE PROJECT MANAGERS, we obsess over the schedule details. We huddle with our teammates to try to anticipate risk factors that could derail our projects. We crunch numbers to see if we can squeeze the project deliverables out of the allocated budget. But we tend to overlook, or ignore, the most prevalent cause of project failure: the human factor.

作为软件项目经理，我们痴迷于进度细节。我们和同事挤在一起，试图预判可能让项目脱轨的风险。我们死抠数字，看能否从分配的预算里挤出项目交付物。但我们往往忽视、甚至无视项目失败最普遍的原因：人的因素。

From errors, to accidents, to out-and-out nonperformance, human failure to perform can often be tied to our tendency to repeat our past behaviors. If it worked successfully for us last time, it should work again. There is an old saying: "For he who is a hammer, every problem is a nail." Psychological research shows that people under the influence of stress may revert to the learning or experiences that are hammer-like, because they found success with them in the past. What is more stressful than undertaking a new software project?

从出错、到事故、再到彻底不胜任，人的失职往往和我们重复过去行为的倾向有关。上次成功了，这次应该也行。有句老话："手里拿着锤子，看什么都像钉子。"心理学研究表明，处于压力下的人可能会退回那些像锤子一样的学习或经验，因为他们过去靠它们成功过。还有什么比做一个新软件项目压力更大？

Because the objective of most projects is to create a new product, service, or solution, agility and flexibility of mind and working style are major positive behaviors to encourage instead of repeating past actions. Following old processes may be counterproductive when you're faced with a new, different challenge. Consider a business analyst who is highly experienced in one formal software project management methodology. Intellectually, he may agree with his developers' explanation of why a more agile approach to software development makes sense. But when faced with time pressures that appear to compromise the project, he may revert to using some favorite techniques that worked well in past, non-software-related experiences.

因为大多数项目的目标是创造新产品、新服务或新方案，思维和工作方式的敏捷与灵活是应当鼓励的积极行为，而不是重复过去的做法。面对全新的、不同的挑战时，遵循旧流程可能适得其反。设想一位精通某种正规软件项目管理方法论的业务分析师。理性上，他可能同意开发解释为什么更敏捷的软件开发方式有道理。但当面对似乎要危及项目的时间压力时，他可能退回到使用那些过去在非软件相关经历中奏效的拿手技巧。

— p.74 —

Bank supervisors report that reversing numbers is a common error, especially when employees are not 100% focused due to work-related or personal stress. Knowing this human tendency, the wise project manager will carefully check estimates, budgets, and other documents for these types of careless, but human, errors.

银行主管报告说，数字写反是常见错误，尤其当员工因为工作或个人压力无法 100% 专注时。明白这种人的倾向后，明智的项目经理会仔细核对估算、预算和其他文档，揪出这类粗心但人之常情的错误。

What leads to stress on your project team? It could be personal, such as having an argument with a spouse before leaving for work, or financial pressures at home. Perhaps there are family worries about health or children. Work-related encounters can also be stress inducing. It could be something as minor as being late to a key stakeholder meeting and forgetting to bring an important document. Or, it could be concerns from job security to worries that the coding and testing for this project cannot be completed on target.

什么会让你的项目团队有压力？可能是个人的：上班前和配偶吵了一架，或是家里的经济压力。也可能是家人健康或孩子方面的担忧。工作中的遭遇也会造成压力。小到参加重要相关方会议迟到、忘带一份重要文件，大到担心工作不保、担心这个项目的编码和测试无法按期完成。

Stress leads to past behavior, not active problem-solving actions. As the software project manager, it is your job to be on the lookout for symptoms of stress that can lead your team members to regress to old behaviors. By having active conversations with them and carefully managing their work environment, you can prevent or help minimize the effects of stress. People are human, so human emotions are natural in the workplace. But only people can develop software. So, nurture and manage your human capital as carefully as you monitor and protect your nonhuman resources.

压力导致的是过去的行为，而不是主动解决问题。作为软件项目经理，你的工作就是警惕压力的征兆——它们会让团队成员退回旧行为。通过主动和他们交谈、仔细管理他们的工作环境，你可以预防或尽量减轻压力的影响。人就是人，工作场所有人的情绪很正常。但只有人能开发软件。所以，请像监控和保护你的非人力资源一样，用心培养和管理你的人力资本。

— p.75 —

Use a Wiki用 Wiki

Adrian Wible · New York, New York, U.S.Adrian Wible · 美国纽约州纽约市

WIKIS ARE A GREAT MECHANISM to centralize access to your project information. Hopefully, the wiki will be updated multiple times daily and will always be open in a window on team members' desktops.

Wiki 是集中管理项目信息访问的绝佳机制。理想情况下，wiki 每天被更新多次，并且在团队成员桌面上始终开着一个窗口。

To prevent you from wasting any precious brain cells that may be needed for the actual project work, I've provided some suggestions for pages you might include on your wiki. While creating these, you are sure to have ideas about customizing the site for your own software project:

为了不浪费你宝贵的脑细胞（那可是要留给真正项目工作的），我列一些建议页面，你可以放进 wiki。创建这些时，你肯定会冒出为自己软件项目定制站点的想法：

  • Stakeholders. Have space for topics such as up-to-the-minute project status, short-term issues, long-term issues, risk, budget tracking, and milestone achievements.
    相关方区。放这些主题：最新项目状态、短期问题、长期问题、风险、预算跟踪、里程碑达成。
  • Developers. Add information such as the connection string to connect to the QA database. Fellow programmers won't waste time trying to locate the code from other random sources. Team members can share information on topics like coding standards, build and deployment procedures, common pitfalls, and use of advanced coding techniques such as dependency injection.
    开发区。放这些信息：连接 QA 数据库的连接字符串。其他程序员不必再从乱七八糟的地方找代码。团队成员可以分享编码规范、构建部署流程、常见坑、以及依赖注入等高级编码技巧。
  • General information. The software project manager should add the help desk phone number, team roles and responsibilities, and individual team member contact information here.
    一般信息。软件项目经理应在这里放帮助台电话、团队角色与职责、每位团队成员的联系方式。
  • Team calendars. Use this site to post team calendars. One great trick is to use an embedded iFrame pointing to a Google calendar.
    团队日历。在这里发布团队日历。一个绝招是用嵌入的 iFrame 指向 Google 日历。
  • Meeting minutes. Archive meeting minutes so the team can easily refresh its memory on the details covered in past meetings. Also, team members can quickly reference the minutes to research or prepare for future meetings.
    会议纪要。归档会议纪要，团队能轻松回顾过去会议的细节。团队成员也能快速查阅纪要，为将来的会议做研究或准备。
— p.76 —
  • Meeting agenda. Set up a process for stakeholders to suggest future agenda items online. Subject, of course, to the approval of the software project manager, the necessity for the item to be presented to the entire team, and the time limitations of the next meeting.
    会议议程。建立一个流程，让相关方在线建议未来的议程项。当然要经软件项目经理批准、判断是否有必要向全团队展示，并受下次会议时间限制。
  • Business analyst. Often this person is not colocated in the developer workspace. This is a perfect space to centralize access to working documents and domain artifacts that can be accessed from multiple locations.
    业务分析师区。这个人常常不和开发坐在一起。这里是集中存放工作文档和领域制品的理想场所，可从多个地点访问。
  • Testers. The organizational structure may separate testing responsibility from the programmer. This site can provide a clearinghouse between the two teams. Post topics like how to use testing tools such as Selenium, QTP, and Quality Center. Bug-tracking procedures can be developed and discussed online, and the final decisions posted here.
    测试区。组织结构可能把测试职责与程序员分开。这个站点可以充当两队之间的交换中心。发布如何使用 Selenium、QTP、Quality Center 等测试工具的主题。bug 跟踪流程可以在线制定和讨论，最终决定贴在这里。

Some tips:

几点建议：

  • Don't duplicate information. If the information lies elsewhere, link to that information instead of copying it into the wiki.
    不要重复信息。如果信息在别处，链接过去，而不是复制进 wiki。
  • Keep an eye on the volume of changes to make sure the information is not getting stale. If it does, people will stop using the wiki.
    关注变更量，确保信息不会过时。一旦过时，人们就会弃用 wiki。
  • Try to make your information real-time-data–driven if possible. Look for project management tools that include a wiki interface to enable creation of charts and status that is driven from the actual project data. This gives real-time status for the work in progress.
    尽量让信息由实时数据驱动。找那些带 wiki 界面的项目管理工具，能从真实项目数据生成图表和状态。这样进行中的工作就有实时状态。

Any time you send project information via email, particularly with file attachments (documents, project plans, budget information, etc.), you should consider whether the team wiki would be a more appropriate place to exchange and archive that information.

每当你通过邮件发送项目信息，特别是带附件（文档、项目计划、预算信息等）时，都该想想：团队 wiki 是不是更适合交换和归档这些信息的地方。

— p.77 —

The Missing Link缺失的一环

Paul Waggoner, MBA, PMP, MCSE, CHP, CHSS · Waukee, Iowa, U.S.Paul Waggoner（MBA, PMP, MCSE, CHP, CHSS）· 美国艾奥瓦州沃基

SOFTWARE PROJECT MANAGERS AGREE that one of their most difficult challenges is keeping team members properly engaged in the details of the project, and on top of their assigned tasks and schedules. They understand that team members are conflicted between the routine, operational responsibilities of processing daily work, troubleshooting problems, coordinating departmental issues, and answering everyday communications, versus completing the time-sensitive work of project development.

软件项目经理都认同，他们最困难的挑战之一，是让团队成员真正投入项目细节，并盯紧分配给自己的任务和进度。他们明白，团队成员夹在中间：一边是处理日常工作、排查问题、协调部门事务、回复日常沟通这些常规运营职责；另一边是完成时间敏感的项目开发工作。

Although being selected for a project team may initially be seen as a compliment, many developers feel that participation on a team is a major distraction from day-to-day duties. When push comes to shove, a developer may openly admit that daily maintenance and support of assigned systems are more important to him/her than performing project task work.

被选进项目团队起初可能被视为一种肯定，但许多开发觉得参加团队是对日常工作的巨大干扰。到了紧要关头，开发可能公开承认：对他/她来说，日常维护和支持所负责的系统，比做项目任务更重要。

As a project manager, your first impulse is to conclude that this person does not belong on the team if your work can't, or won't, be given a clear priority. However, most organizations have limited numbers of subject matter experts (SMEs), so changing team members or locating a more dedicated one may not be an option.

作为项目经理，你的第一反应可能是：如果项目工作不能、也不愿被给予明确优先级，这个人就不该待在团队里。然而，大多数组织的领域专家（SME）数量有限，换团队成员或找个更投入的人可能不是可行选项。

Here are a few simple suggestions to help with this problem:

以下是几个简单建议，帮你应对这个问题：

  • Make sure all management levels support the goals and objectives of the project.
    确保各管理层都支持项目的目的和目标。
  • Modify the subject matter expert job description to include "perform as team member on various projects as needed," instead of "perform other duties as assigned."
    修改领域专家的岗位描述，加入「按需在各项目中担任团队成员」，而不是「履行分配的其他职责」。
  • Have management and Human Resources emphasize this change, and make sure all supervisors weigh project activity achievements heavily in future performance evaluations.
    让管理层和人力资源强调这一变化，并确保所有主管在未来绩效评估中给项目活动成绩高权重。
— p.78 —
  • At the beginning of each new project, the software project manager, the departmental manager or supervisor, the sponsor, or another key stakeholder should send out a personalized communiqué inviting each team member to participate in the project. This letter or email should explain the high-level objectives of the project being undertaken, and the high-level responsibilities of this specific team member.
    每个新项目开始时，软件项目经理、部门经理或主管、发起人或其他关键相关方应发出一份个性化文告，邀请每位团队成员参与项目。这封信或邮件应说明所开展项目的高层目标，以及这位团队成员的高层职责。
  • Announce that at the successful conclusion of this project, each team member will receive a Certificate of Recognition and Achievement suitable for framing. Note that a second copy will be placed in his/her Human Resources file to be referenced during quarterly performance reviews.
    宣布：项目成功收尾时，每位团队成员将获得一份值得装裱的表彰与成就证书。并注明副本将存入其人力资源档案，供季度绩效评审参考。
  • The departmental manager's boss should make it clear that projects advance organizational goals at an even more important level than the routine information technology tasks do.
    部门经理的上级应明确：项目推进组织目标的层级，比日常 IT 任务更重要。
  • The executive should specifically request that the departmental manager help the project team member free up time on a regular basis to complete the project activities, even if his regular tasks must be temporarily off-loaded to another member of the IT group.
    高管应明确要求部门经理帮助项目团队成员定期腾出时间完成项目活动，即使他的常规任务必须临时转交给 IT 组的另一位成员。

It should be clearly understood that those who successfully participate in projects are "going the extra mile" for the organization and should be recognized and rewarded. Those who participate successfully in large or small projects should be singled out for praise. As they say in the agile world, this puts the "art of the possible" in proper perspective, aligning organizational objectives with employee motivations.

应当清楚地认识到：成功参与项目的人是在为组织"多走一里路"，应当被认可和奖励。成功参与大大小小项目的人应当被单独点名表扬。正如敏捷圈所说，这让"可能的艺术"摆对了位置，把组织目标和员工动机对齐起来。

— p.79 —

Estimate, Estimate, Estimate估算，反复估算

Richard Sheridan · Ann Arbor, Michigan, U.S.Richard Sheridan · 美国密歇根州安娜堡

SO OFTEN IN PROJECT MANAGEMENT, we get an estimate for a project at the beginning of the project (when we know the least) and then never revisit that estimate during the course of the project (when we know more than we did at the beginning). Worse, we never compare our original estimate with actual results to hone our future skills.

在项目管理中，我们常常在项目开始时（我们知道得最少的时候）拿到一个估算，然后在项目过程中（我们比开始时知道得更多的时候）再也不回头看那个估算。更糟的是，我们从不把原始估算和实际结果对比，来打磨未来的技能。

In our practice at my organization, we estimate once a week on every project. Even for those tasks we have previously estimated but haven't worked on yet, we estimate again. Why do we do this? There are several reasons:

在我们组织的实践中，每个项目每周估算一次。即便是那些我们之前估过、但还没动手做的任务，也要重新估算。为什么这么做？有几个原因：

  • We get better at estimating the more we do it.
    估算做得越多，我们越擅长。
  • Sometimes we now know more and that helps our estimating.
    有时候我们现在知道得更多了，这有助于估算。
  • Sometimes we learn we didn't know as much as we thought we did, and that helps our estimating.
    有时候我们发现自己并不像以为的懂得那么多，这也有助于估算。
  • Often when a new technology is involved, early estimates have "fear" built in; as we learn more about the new technology, the fear-based component lessens.
    当涉及新技术时，早期估算里往往掺着「恐惧」；随着我们对新技术了解加深，恐惧成分会减少。
  • Estimating is a great "conversation" in our world, since we estimate as a group activity.
    在我们这里，估算是一场很棒的「对话」，因为它是团队活动。

Finally, the best way to get better at estimating is to make sure you also keep track of actuals so that the team gets feedback on how well it did in estimating. My only warning: you can't use this information to punish the team! True accountability around estimating doesn't involve getting people to hit their estimate, but rather to have them warn you as soon as they think they are going to miss.

最后，提升估算能力最好的办法，是同时记录实际值，让团队得到自己估算准确度的反馈。我唯一的警告：你不能用这些信息惩罚团队！围绕估算的真正问责，不是逼人去命中估算，而是让他们一旦觉得要延期就立刻提醒你。

— p.80 —

Here is a simple game you can play to drive home the power of estimating and feedback. Get three different empty jars of increasing size and fill them with jelly beans. Record how many jelly beans it takes to fill up every jar. Get together a group you are trying to teach about estimating and ask members to estimate the number of jelly beans in the smallest jar. When I teach this, I have people work in pairs. Give them only a short time to come up with an estimate and then have them write it down. Collect the data by having each pair read its estimates aloud. Write the estimates down on a whiteboard or flipchart. Do the same for the second and third jars of jelly beans.

这里有个简单的游戏，可以让你深刻体会估算和反馈的力量。找三个大小递增的空罐子，装满软糖。记下每个罐子实际装了多少颗。把你要教估算的人凑成一组，让他们猜最小罐子里有多少颗软糖。我教的时候让大家两人一组。给他们很短时间给出估算，然后写下来。让每组大声读出自己的估算，把数据收集起来，写在白板或翻页纸上。对第二、第三个罐子重复同样的事。

Finally, tell the group members that this is a good way to do estimating, thank them for their input, and ask if there are any questions before you move on. It never fails. Someone will ask how many jelly beans there actually are in each jar. They want to know! Let them dangle a while and then tell them how silly they are. After all, it's just a jar of jelly beans. Now you have them right where you want them. Ask them how many times they've had the data to give feedback to their team on far more important topics and they scoffed and dismissed it as unimportant. Overlooking feedback to their teams will not happen again.

最后，告诉大家这就是做估算的好办法，感谢他们的参与，问有没有问题再继续。每次都这样：一定有人问每个罐子里到底有多少颗。他们想知道！让他们吊一会儿胃口，然后告诉他们有多傻。不过是一罐软糖而已。现在你把他们拿捏住了。问他们：有多少次，他们手里有数据，可以就重要得多的话题给团队反馈，却嗤之以鼻、觉得不重要。从此，他们不会再忽视给团队的反馈。

— p.81 —

Developers Unite—PMOs Are Advancing开发们团结起来——PMO 正在逼近

Angelo Valle · Rio de Janeiro, BrazilAngelo Valle · 巴西里约热内卢

IF YOU'RE A SOFTWARE DEVELOPER, you are probably convinced that a more responsive, adaptable framework is your best chance of producing working software. Unfortunately, the rest of the world is moving to have a more standardized approach throughout all departments. This is good news for everyone except software developers.

如果你是软件开发，你大概坚信：一个响应更快、更灵活的框架，是你产出可用软件的最大希望。不幸的是，世界其他地方正在所有部门推行更标准化的做法。这对所有人都是好消息——除了软件开发。

A recently emerging concept in organizational structure is the project management office (PMO). This global phenomenon tasks a small group of individuals with the supervision and support of enterprise projects and programs. The group's purpose is to introduce consistency in documents and templates, standardize reporting processes, and provide a uniform way to add business value through projects.

组织结构中一个新近兴起的概念是项目管理办公室（PMO）。这个全球现象把监督和支持企业项目与项目集的任务交给一小群人。这个小组的目的是让文档和模板保持一致、标准化报告流程，并提供一种统一的方式通过项目增加业务价值。

PMOs are intended to be centers of intelligence and coordination. They link strategic business objectives to employees' actions within departmental projects through unified portfolio management, program management, and project management practices. This is a good thing for your job security. The PMO's functions within the business can be:

PMO 应当是情报和协调中心。它们通过统一的项目组合管理、项目集管理和项目管理实践，把战略业务目标与员工在部门项目中的行动联系起来。这对你的职场稳定是好事。PMO 在业务中的职能可以是：

  • Strategic. In this role, the members of the Project Management Office complete functions of identification, selection, and prioritization of the projects that are most closely aligned with the organization's strategic planning.
    战略性。在这个角色下，PMO 成员负责识别、筛选并优先排序与组织战略规划最契合的项目。
  • Directive. To fulfill their directive responsibilities, PMO employees define guidelines, standards, and templates. They evaluate and choose how software project managers should apply the best practices, tools, techniques, and software to successfully complete the goals of their development teams.
    指导性。为履行指导职责，PMO 员工定义指南、标准和模板。他们评估并选择软件项目经理应如何运用最佳实践、工具、技术和软件，以成功完成开发团队的目标。
— p.82 —
  • Supportive. The PMO provides support to team members and project managers. This may manifest itself as training classes, adjusting templates and documents to make them work in all departments, or working with a project manager on staffing or other human resource issues.
    支持性。PMO 为团队成员和项目经理提供支持。可能表现为培训课程、调整模板和文档使其在各部门都能用，或与项目经理一起处理人员配置和其他人力资源问题。

Project Management Offices are not identical from corporation to corporation around the world. Each business is at a different developmental stage with its project management practices. So, the common name of PMO may encompass numerous hybrid responsibilities drawn from the aforementioned list, or unique ones not mentioned.

世界各地公司的 PMO 并不相同。每家企业的项目管理实践处于不同发展阶段。因此，PMO 这个通称可能包含上述清单中混合而来的众多职责，或未提及的独特职责。

The PMO provides guidance in suitable standardized and validated tools, techniques, and software, thereby reducing problems due to uncertainty and the growing emphasis on cheaper/better/faster projects. The PMO applies a standardized methodology where necessary and effective: project identification, data collection, analysis, information gathering, distribution, reporting, risk management, procurement, quality, and other project management knowledge areas such as documentation and communications.

PMO 在合适、标准化、经过验证的工具、技术和软件方面提供指导，从而减少因不确定性以及对"更便宜/更好/更快"项目日益强调而产生的问题。PMO 在必要且有效的地方应用标准化方法：项目识别、数据收集、分析、信息收集、分发、报告、风险管理、采购、质量，以及文档和沟通等其他项目管理知识领域。

The theme of economic success through a PMO model is a hot topic in international congresses, seminars, and recently published papers. Academic discussions are prolific, because of a growing need to match university experiences with actual "real world" practices. The students of today are the developers of tomorrow.

通过 PMO 模式取得经济成功这个主题，在国际大会、研讨会和新近发表的论文中是热门话题。学术讨论层出不穷，因为越来越需要把大学经历与真实世界的实践对接。今天的学生就是明天的开发。

PMOs are here to stay. If you are currently a software developer, you should be proactive in opening a dialog with your PMO. Communicate your professional success stories and the uniqueness of the software development process. If you don't, you are liable to be saddled with methods, documentation requirements, and procedures that don't fit your needs. Fast, good, high-quality software is in everyone's best interest.

PMO 会长期存在。如果你现在是软件开发，应当主动和 PMO 展开对话。讲你职业成功的故事，讲软件开发过程的独特性。不这样做，你就可能被加上不适合你需求的方法、文档要求和流程。快速、优良、高质量的软件符合所有人的利益。

— p.83 —

Value Results, Not Just Effort看重结果，而不只是苦劳

Venkat Subramaniam · Broomfield, Colorado, U.S.Venkat Subramaniam · 美国科罗拉多州布鲁姆菲尔德

DEVELOPING SOFTWARE TAKES A LOT OF EFFORT. However, if you hear someone brag, "I work on an application with over 3 million lines of code," ask him or her how many of those lines of code are really needed. Often, extra code is added with some perceived extensibility in mind. Extensibility is important, but if not done correctly, it can have the opposite effect. It can delay your current project.

开发软件要花很大力气。然而，如果你听到有人吹嘘："我在一个有三百万行代码的应用上工作。"问他/她这些代码里有多少是真的需要的。额外代码常常是想着某种可扩展性加进去的。可扩展性重要，但做得不对会适得其反，会拖慢你当前的项目。

* Extensibility: A systems design principle where future growth is taken into consideration. The ability to create and implement additional features is maximized while coding the currently needed functionality.* 可扩展性：一种系统设计原则，把未来的增长考虑在内。在编码当前所需功能时，把创建和实现额外功能的能力最大化。

Extra, out-of-scope code is a symptom of software project managers who reward only extra time and extra effort. If you routinely insist that the programmers work long hours, be sure they are actually producing additional, useable results.

额外的、超出范围的代码，是那些只奖励加班和苦劳的软件项目经理的症状。如果你习惯坚持让程序员长时间工作，请确认他们真的产出了额外、可用的成果。

I like my lawn to be green, and rely on my sprinkler system to water it every day. My first summer in Colorado, I noticed that one of my maple trees had lost most of its leaves. Assuming that the hot and arid conditions were the reason, I watered longer but noticed no improvement. The expert I consulted asked me, "How frequently and how long do you water?" Hearing my answer, he said, "That's the problem! Reduce the duration and frequency by half, and you will see improvement." I was killing the tree with excessive water. Having slightly less water actually helps these trees. It builds their resistance and helps their growth. Two weeks after following his advice, my tree was healthy and full of leaves.

我喜欢草坪绿油油，靠自动喷淋系统每天浇水。在科罗拉多的第一个夏天，我注意到一棵枫树叶子掉了大半。我以为是炎热干燥所致，就延长浇水时间，但没见好转。我请教的专家问我："你多久浇一次、每次浇多久？"听完我的回答，他说："问题就在这！把时长和频率都减一半，你就会看到改善。"我是用水过多把树害了。少浇一点水反而有助于这些树，能增强抵抗力、帮助生长。按他的建议两周后，我的树健康了、满树是叶。

— p.84 —

Your programmers are like maple trees when it comes to work time. Give them small, but adequate amounts of time and fewer broadly defined tasks, and they flourish. Give them larger task chunks and ask them to routinely work extra hours, and they begin to wilt. Plus, they tend to overwrite and complicate the code, since they have too much time on their hands.

你的程序员在工作时间方面就像枫树。给他们小而充足的时间、更少的大而化之的任务，他们就枝繁叶茂。给他们大块任务、要求经常加班，他们就开始蔫。而且，因为手上时间太多，他们还会过度写代码、把代码搞复杂。

I worked for a manager who focused on how long people worked. Working a Saturday morning, or staying late in the evening, was more important to him than what employees were actually producing. It is impossible to be a productive and effective programmer for 12 hours or more a day.

我曾为一个只盯着人工作时长的经理干活。周六上午来加班、晚上熬到很晚，对他来说比员工实际产出什么更重要。一个程序员每天高效产出 12 小时以上是不可能的。

In another group, the manager kept us to a traditional eight-hour work schedule. Yes, there were days we stayed late, but those were exceptions rather than the norm. Employees knew they were not required to work long hours but had to provide their committed deliverables on schedule. So, we were focused and less distracted, prioritized our work well, and used our time effectively. Even though developer capabilities were about the same in both groups, we got more accomplished in the second group than in the one where we worked to exhaustion.

在另一个组，经理让我们守传统的八小时工作制。确实有几天我们留得晚，但那是例外而非常态。员工知道不必长时间工作，但必须按计划交付承诺的成果。于是我们专注、少分心、排好优先级、有效利用时间。尽管两个组的开发能力差不多，第二个组完成的事比那个把我们榨干的组多。

Encourage programmers to report the progress they make, rather than how long they work. Let them know that you care about getting results rather than keeping track of how long they spent at the computer. Once your team members realize that you are a results-oriented manager and not a "put in hours" manager, their focus will shift to achieving results rather than merely clocking hours at work.

鼓励程序员汇报取得的进展，而不是工作了多久。让他们知道你关心的是拿到结果，而不是记录他们在电脑前坐了多久。一旦团队成员意识到你是结果导向的经理，而不是"拼工时"的经理，他们的注意力就会转向取得结果，而不只是在班上打卡凑时长。

— p.85 —

Software Failure Is Organizational Failure软件失败是组织的失败

Brian Sletten · Beverly Hills, California, U.S.Brian Sletten · 美国加州比佛利山

WE ALWAYS BLAME DEVELOPERS when things go wrong with software projects in an organization. When deadlines are missed, or when what is delivered has more bugs than an entomologist's wildest fantasy, it may seem that the team is not good enough, smart enough, productive enough, or up to the challenge. While individual teams may deserve a fair amount of criticism, you cannot forget that successful software projects require active and adequate participation by all stakeholders.

组织里软件项目出问题时，我们总是责怪开发。错过截止日，或交付的东西 bug 多到昆虫学家做梦都想不到，看起来好像团队不够好、不够聪明、不够高效、扛不住挑战。虽然单个团队确实该挨不少批评，但你不能忘记：成功的软件项目需要所有相关方积极、充分的参与。

Everyone's participation is crucial, because in order to stave off failure, you need to know who is building what, when, and why. You need to add business functionality in deliberate, prioritized ways. You need to catch problems with poorly captured and expressed requirements. You need to nip latent impediments in the bud by spotting people who are potential blockers, noting communication failures, and soothing overwhelmed (but overeager) development teams.

每个人的参与都至关重要，因为要避免失败，你得知道谁在什么时候造什么、为什么。你要有计划、分优先级地增加业务功能。你要抓住需求捕捉和表达不清的问题。你要通过识别潜在的"拦路虎"、注意沟通失败、安抚不堪重负（却又过于急切）的开发团队，把潜在障碍掐灭在萌芽状态。

Developing software requires valid metrics, clear communication, and engaged business and executive stakeholders. They must be involved in software delivery efforts and assume partial responsibility for both positive and negative outcomes. The software project manager needs to measure and track success and failure records. Teams that consistently deliver can be trusted to do so again. Teams that seldom deliver require more oversight, further training, and realignment, or perhaps some members must be shown the door.

开发软件需要有效的指标、清晰的沟通、以及投入的业务和高管相关方。他们必须参与软件交付工作，对好结果和坏结果都承担部分责任。软件项目经理需要衡量并跟踪成功与失败记录。持续交付的团队可以被信任再次交付。很少交付的团队需要更多监督、进一步培训和重新校准，或者某些成员必须请走人。

* Releases: The agile method creates specific functionality within several short time frames. During each period, requirements analysis, planning, design, coding, unit testing, and acceptance testing are performed. At the end, a workable feature is "released" to the customer.* 发布：敏捷方法在若干短时间框内创造特定功能。每个时间段内做需求分析、计划、设计、编码、单元测试和验收测试。时间框结束时，一个可用的功能「发布」给客户。

However, allow software teams time to clean up their own messes. As they rush toward various releases, they will incur what wiki pioneer Ward Cunningham calls "technical debt." Like real debt, if it is not paid down consistently and responsibly, it will become unwieldy and require too much attention to service.

然而，要给软件团队时间清理自己的烂摊子。在赶向一个个发布的过程中，他们会欠下 wiki 先驱 Ward Cunningham 所说的"技术债"。和真债一样，如果不定期、负责任地偿还，它会变得难以驾驭、需要太多精力去伺候。

— p.86 —

Each iteration of work should include new business functionality, as well as a sanctioned effort to refactor some of the hacks that inevitably show up in the code. This is neither a license to goof off, nor the sign of a bad team. It is simply a programming reality that must be routinely addressed with full support from the executive stakeholders. The organization must commit to tracking industry trends, acquiring tools, and adopting practices that demonstrate productive influences on how programmers work.

每个迭代都应既包含新业务功能，也包含一份经批准的精力，用来重构代码中不可避免出现的 hack。这不是摸鱼的许可证，也不是坏团队的标志。它只是编程的现实，必须在高管相关方的全力支持下例行处理。组织必须承诺跟踪行业趋势、采购工具、并采纳那些被证明对程序员工作方式有积极影响的实践。

Encourage developers to expand their knowledge, both on and off the clock. Playing around with new tools, being trained, attending high-value conferences, and reading books and blogs are all necessary components of the constant effort required by this field. Organizing team lunches where members share knowledge and promote new ideas is a great, inexpensive way to foster growth. Software engineers who feel supported by their employers tend to be more loyal and willing to go the extra mile. They are also more likely to be able and ready to respond to changes in requirements and technical landscapes.

鼓励开发在上班和下班时间扩展知识。摆弄新工具、接受培训、参加高价值会议、读书和看博客，都是这个领域所要求的持续努力的必要组成。组织团队午餐，让成员分享知识、催生新想法，是培养成长的绝佳而廉价的方式。感到雇主支持的软件工程师往往更忠诚、更愿意多走一里路。他们也更有可能有能力、有准备应对需求和技术格局的变化。

The software industry has a lot of work to do to help its practitioners be more consistent in the delivery of high-quality, on-time releases. Organizations that build software must be engaged in the process at all levels to improve their own chances for continued, repeatable success.

软件行业还有很多工作要做，以帮助从业者更稳定地交付高质量、按时的发布。造软件的组织必须在各个层级参与这个过程，以提高自己持续、可重复成功的概率。

— p.87 —
